omar: Quick sync — thinking through KV cache *persistence* and keying when kernels, drivers, or models change. Do we want persisted blobs to survive kernel picks/driver bumps and model rollouts, or always invalidate? Need concrete key schema + invalidation rules.

sylvia: I think persisted blobs should survive *compatible* changes but we must version them. Key components we need: model_id@model_hash, kernel_semantic_id (not raw kernel binary id), runtime_driver_ver, quant_profile_id, seq_len_bin, prefix_hash. Example key: `sha256(model_hash + ':' + kernel_semantic_id + ':' + driver_ver + ':' + seq_bin + ':' + prefix_hash)`.

jess: +1 on semantic kernel id. Practical constraints: if we include raw kernel build id, every driver patch explodes keys. Instead maintain a kernel compatibility map (kernel_semantic_id -> set of compatible raw_kernel_ids). Persist only when raw_kernel_id ∈ compatible_set. For storage: persist to shared object store with small manifest JSON next to blob containing the metadata above and a small refcount/last_access.

ravi: Data point from benchmarking: shared prefix cache gave ~15% p95 token latency reduction on our 8k prompt workload. After a driver bump (520 -> 522) we saw ~8% of hits turn into misses because kernel selection changed slightly (different matmul path). So versioning matters.

eng-bot: perf-alert: CI perf-regression on branch `autotune-cache-v2` (commit d4f7a1e): p50 +4ms, kv_hit_rate -6pp vs main. See: https://ci.internal/reports/3456 :warning:

omar: Proposal sketch: 1) define key schema like Sylvia suggested, 2) maintain a small manifest per blob with: model_hash, kernel_semantic_id, compatible_raw_kernels[], driver_compat_range, seq_len_bin, persisted_at, access_count 3) persist only for top-N (by traffic) model+kernel_semantic combos to limit S3 churn 4) eviction = TTL + LFU + occasional compaction job 5) invalidation triggers: explicit model hash bump, kernel_semantic_id bump, driver compatibility range mismatch, or manual admin purge.

sylvia: One more: add a `compatibility_version` numeric field that autotuner increments when we change kernel-selection heuristics in ways that might change KV cache layout. That lets us expire obsolete blobs without tying to raw driver version constantly.

jess: I'll run an experiment matrix: seq_len_bins [<=64, 65-128, 129-256, 257-512, >512] × archs [Ampere, Blackwell] × driver_versions [520, 522, 524] to capture where kernel_semantic_id diverges. Expect divergence >256 tokens. Will post heatmap results tomorrow.

omar: Operational ask: eng-sre — can we estimate monthly storage + egress if we persist top-50 combos with avg blob size ~8MB? Also need a quick migration path: when compatibility_version bumps, autotuner should have a `rehydrate` step that prefetches top-k blobs for warmed nodes.

ravi: Also consider a thin on-node compatibility shim: if cached prefix is same shape and dtype, allow reusing KV even if kernel binary differs, but validate with checksum-first token generation on a small prefix to detect subtle semantic errors. Tradeoff: slight extra compute at warmup.

eng-bot: ack: muted perf alerts for branch `autotune-cache-v2` (requested by omar).

sylvia: I'll draft a small manifest proto and key-format doc this afternoon and push a PR. Will include compatibility_version semantics and pseudo-code for generating kernel_semantic_id.

omar: Thanks — tagging @eng-sre for storage/egress estimate and @product-infra for any compliance notes (persisting prefixes might touch data retention rules). :thinking:

jess: FYI sample key pseudocode I'll test: ```python
def make_kv_key(model_hash, kernel_semantic_id, driver_tag, seq_bin, prefix_hash):
    raw = f"{model_hash}:{kernel_semantic_id}:{driver_tag}:{seq_bin}:{prefix_hash}"
    return sha256(raw).hexdigest()
```

omar: OK good plan. Volunteers: Sylvia -> key + manifest, Jess -> perf matrix, Ravi -> small validation shim prototype, Omar -> migration + policy doc. I'll assemble into an RFC once we have initial numbers.

eng-bot: Note: direct admin purge endpoint exists at `/admin/kv/purge` for emergency invalidation. Use with caution.

jess: 👍 will post numbers in a follow-up thread.
